rationale: Internally consistent and correctly signed, but it is a single-leg component swap on the archive's already-tested WeakestLinkProfitSolvency (identical MIN combiner, identical industry-ranked profitability leg, only the solvency leg changed from net cash/assets to cash+CFO/current liabilities), so the expected incremental information over the existing 3.56-t result is small and the two constructs will be highly correlated.

SUMRANK of two ratios sharing the same denominator (lct) is close to a monotone re-expression of the already-tested EbitdaPlusCashRunway rather than a genuine decomposition, and the cash leg is a direct restatement of the published cash-holdings/liquidity anomaly, so the "attributable profitability contribution" claim is not actually identified by this construction.

The core term Δwcap/revt is the classic working-capital accruals anomaly (Sloan 1996) in only lightly disguised form, and the short-term-debt gate reproduces the exact conditioning structure of the archive's CashConversionUnderMaturityPressure, so this is largely a known effect re-wrapped in an existing failed-slope interaction.

This is the well-documented book-tax difference anomaly (Lev-Nissim, Hanlon) in crude form, and the expression contradicts the hypothesis in two ways — txt is total tax expense including the deferred component, so it is not the "cash-verified" measure claimed (txpd would be), and pairing pre-depreciation, pre-interest EBITDA against a post-everything tax line makes the rank gap largely a proxy for capital intensity and leverage rather than unvalidated profit.

The gross-margin channel is a genuinely different economic mechanism from the aggregate ROA trend that failed in LeveredTurnaroundTrend and the expression's sign is coherent (non-negative leverage rank preserves the z-score sign), though it reuses a leverage-gating structure that has now produced weak or wrong-signed results twice in the archive, so prior odds are modest.

Adding depreciation to the obligation denominator is a substantive, economically motivated fix to the vanishing-denominator problem that forced heavy winsorization in the archive's best-slope signal, and it should raise coverage — but note the construct changes meaning across the debt distribution (for near-debt-free firms it degenerates to EBITDA/depreciation, a capital-intensity measure rather than a solvency one), which should be checked in the diagnostics.
